1) Private connectivity: We prefer AWS PrivateLink for vendor endpoints to avoid NAT and maintain flow logs. Does Redwood support PrivateLink endpoints for your Hosted API, or would this require Redwood Private in our VPC?

2) IP allowlist: If PrivateLink is supported, do you still provide static outbound IP ranges for egress (for calls originating inside our VPC to other external services)? Our security team needs the ranges to add to third-party allowlists.

3) DNS: We need to know whether DNS will resolve to private endpoint IPs inside our VPC (split-horizon) vs. external IPs for dev/test. Any best practices?

4) mTLS: We prefer mTLS for client authentication. Can your SDK be configured to use client certs for auth, or is that only supported in Redwood Private? Also curious about cert rotation mechanics.

Hi Alice — great questions. High-level answers below; I can expand each item in a short tech note.

1) PrivateLink support: Redwood Hosted does not currently publish AWS PrivateLink endpoints for multitenant hosted customers. For PrivateLink we typically onboard customers via Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane or private deployment) where we create ENIs/PrivateLink endpoints in the customer's account or a shared VPC. Option: for early PoC we can offer a transit-style setup where requests from your VPC egress through a dedicated NAT in our Dedicated footprint, but that requires a Dedicated contract and specific routing rules.

2) IP allowlist / egress ranges: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can provide static egress IP ranges. For Hosted (multitenant) we publish a set of dynamic ranges (regionally scoped) but we do not guarantee static per-customer IPs. I'll attach the current dedicated egress CIDR list in the tech note.

3) DNS split-horizon: In Private deployments we can configure internal DNS to resolve service endpoints to private IPs (split-horizon). For Hosted, split-horizon is not available — you'd hit public endpoints, unless you route through PrivateLink/Private deployment. For PoC, many customers map a CNAME in their private hosted zone to an IP/endpoint we provide in the Private deployment.

4) mTLS and SDK auth: mTLS is supported in Redwood Private and Dedicated setups. SDKs can be configured to use client certs for service-to-service calls when the deployment is private. For Hosted API we offer short-lived JWT tokens (issuer + refresh) and optional function-level API keys. Cert rotation: for Private we support both customer-supplied certs (you push to our API/secret store) and an automated rotation option (let us manage certs via ACME-style flow). Rotation cadence is configurable; recommended 90 days.

I'll put together a concise tech note (with sample iptables/security-group configs, example DNS records, and a short mTLS handshake flow) and target EOD tomorrow.

Best,
